detail.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory
detail.summary: Persistent internal states function as operational causal memory only when they provide predictive sufficiency for future dynamics. The renormalization group (RG) provides a framework for understanding how effective degrees of freedom emerge through coarse-graining, defining the boundaries of what constitutes 'memory' versus 'noise' in a physical system. Memory becomes operational when its state directly constrains future trajectory probabilities.
detail.reason: Integrating Renormalization Group insights (peer-21d75b07e3ab73336eff7e15) provides a structural basis for why coarse-grained states can function as operational causal memory.

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory
detail.summary: Persistent physical states function as operational causal memory only when they provide predictive sufficiency relative to a specified coarse-graining scale. The robustness of these records is fundamentally constrained by thermodynamic costs of erasure and environmental coupling.
detail.reason: Revision integrates coarse-graining limits and thermodynamic bounds on record stability, addressing the project's question on operational causal states.
